name: Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: wildlife sanctuary and bushwalking area in the Brindabellas, the ACT's second-largest park after Namadgi; kangaroos, koalas, platypus and bird displays.

name: Tidbinbilla Visitor Centre
note: Visitor centre: entry point for Tidbinbilla Nature Reserve, with a gift shop, displays and the start of the Birrigai and Congwarra trails.

name: Birrigai Time Trail
note: Walk: 3 km mostly flat trail from the Tidbinbilla visitor centre to the Birrigai Rock Shelter, an Aboriginal heritage site.

name: Birrigai Rock Shelter
note: Heritage site: Aboriginal rock shelter at the end of the Birrigai Time Trail, with artefacts said to be over 25,000 years old.

name: Gibraltar Peak
note: Peak: 8.2 km steep walk in Tidbinbilla to a summit with panoramic views over Canberra and the reserve.

name: Camels Hump
note: Walk: Tidbinbilla trail with views over Canberra; no distance or grade found in the sources read.

name: Sanctuary Loop
note: Wildlife walk: easy 2.5 km loop through Tidbinbilla's wildlife sanctuary, a place to see rock-wallabies, platypus and echidnas.

name: Church Rock Heritage Loop
note: Walk: 2.5 km loop past late-19th-century ruins in Tidbinbilla.

name: Turkey Hill Trail
note: Short walk: 500 m climb to Turkey Hill with granite boulders and mountain views.

name: Congwarra Trail
note: Family walk: 3–4 km trail from the visitor centre to the nature discovery playground.

name: Canberra Deep Space Communication Complex
note: Science site: NASA deep-space antenna complex at Tidbinbilla with a visitor centre, open weekends (school holidays daily).

name: Honeysuckle Creek Tracking Station
note: Historic site: former NASA Apollo tracking station in Namadgi with remnants of the site; the 26 m dish is a landmark.

name: Orroral Valley Tracking Station
note: Historic site: former NASA Earth station ruins in Namadgi, start of the Orroral Valley Circuit.

name: Corin Forest
note: Operator: forest resort in Paddys River with snow play, an alpine slide and bobsled, and a lodge and dining area.

name: Gibraltar Falls
note: Waterfall: one of the ACT's largest, a drop of over 50 m, with a lookout, barbecue and picnic area off Corin Road.

name: Namadgi Visitor Centre
note: Visitor centre: Namadgi National Park's visitor centre on Naas Road, where visitors ask about the park's walks.

name: Namadgi National Park
note: National park: the ACT's only national park, about 47% of the territory, with walks, mountain bike trails, historic huts, rock art and the northern end of the Australian Alps.

name: Australian Alps Walking Track
note: Long-distance trail: the northernmost section of the 640 km Australian Alps Walking Track runs through Namadgi.

name: Booroomba Rocks
note: Rock formation and walk: 2.5 km return grade-4 walk to granite tors with a cliff edge; also a rock climbing site.

name: Mount Gingera
note: Peak: 14.5 km return walk from Mount Franklin Road to the summit; a winter snow sports area.

name: Mount Franklin (Australian Capital Territory)
note: Peak and historic site: 3 km walk to the summit with the Franklin Shelter and a historic skiing display.

name: Bimberi Peak
note: Peak: highest point in the ACT (1,911 m) in the remote Bimberi wilderness of Namadgi.

name: Yankee Hat
note: Rock art site: mountain on Old Boboyan Road with an Aboriginal rock painting of a kangaroo, dingos, emus and humans; also a car park for the Gudgenby circuit.

name: Settlers Track
note: Walk: 6 km loop from Boboyan Road through pastoral sites, with a 9 km option to Waterhole Hut.

name: Orroral Valley Circuit
note: Walk: 19 km loop from the Orroral Tracking Station, taking about a day, in either direction.

name: Orroral Campground
note: Campground: Namadgi campground near the Orroral Homestead and Orroral Valley trails.

name: Honeysuckle Campground
note: Campground: Namadgi campground near the Honeysuckle Creek tracking station site.

name: Ginini Flats Wetlands Ramsar Site
note: Wetland: the ACT's only Ramsar-listed wetland, protected by alpine vegetation, reached on Namadgi's high country tracks.

name: Mount Ginini
note: Peak and ski area: the Ginini Flats high country and Mount Ginini ski area in Namadgi.

name: Mount Coree
note: Peak: a Namadgi mountain with a Wikipedia article; no visitor source found naming it as a place to go.

name: Hospital Hill Lookout
note: Lookout: Boboyan Road lookout with interpretive signs on the mountain's geography and views.

name: Brandy Flat Hut
note: Historic hut: 1900s hut on the Brandy Flat Firetrail, a stopover for cyclists and bushwalkers.

name: Gudgenby Homestead
note: Historic homestead: one of the region's oldest huts, built in 1845, dismantled in 1964 and stored for re-erection; on Boboyan Road.

name: Orroral Homestead
note: Historic hut: 1860s homestead, the oldest hut in Namadgi and one of the best conserved, with information signs.

name: Brayshaws and Westermans Homesteads
note: Historic homesteads: two pastoral-era homesteads on Boboyan Road, a stop on the Settlers Track.

name: Horse Gully Hut
note: Historic hut: Second World War-era hut near Mount Clear Campground.

name: Bendora Dam
note: Dam: 1961 thin-arch concrete dam, the first of its type built in Australia, with some lookouts.

name: Corin Dam
note: Dam: Canberra water supply dam in the Corin Dam Road area, beside Corin Forest.

name: Cotter Dam
note: Dam: Canberra water supply dam on the Cotter River.

name: Bendora Arboretum
note: Arboretum: 1940 experimental tree plantings with 52 species, popular with bushwalkers; a rough, isolated drive.

name: Mount Rogers (Australian Capital Territory)
note: Peak: mountain with a Wikipedia article and OpenStreetMap peak node; no visitor source found naming it as a place to go.

name: Cotter Reserve
note: Riverside reserve: the Cotter Recreation Area of the Murrumbidgee River Corridor, with picnic and camping sites on the Cotter River.

name: Cotter Campground
note: Campground: camping, picnic shelters and barbecues at 1691 Cotter Road, a base for Stromlo Forest Park.

name: Cotter Avenue
note: Picnic site: electric barbecues, shelter, toilets and an adventure playground on the Cotter River.

name: Cotter Bend
note: Riverside picnic spot: sandy beach with electric barbecues on the Cotter River.

name: Casuarina Sands
note: Riverside beach: sandy Murrumbidgee beach in the Cotter Recreation Area for picnics, fishing and walks.

name: Point Hut Crossing
note: Picnic area: shady river crossing with sandy beaches at the south end of the Murrumbidgee Discovery Track.

name: Uriarra Crossing
note: Picnic area: both banks of the Murrumbidgee at Uriarra, popular with birdwatchers.

name: Swamp Creek
note: Picnic area: within the Uriarra Crossing Recreation Area on the Murrumbidgee.

name: Angle Crossing
note: River site: the southernmost point of the Murrumbidgee within the ACT, reached by the river corridor.

name: Murrays Corner
note: River site: Murrumbidgee corridor site listed by Parks ACT; its page has little content, so visitor value is unclear.

name: Pine Island Reserve
note: Riverside reserve: pine-tree reserve on the Murrumbidgee with swimming, fishing and kayaking, and a start point for the Murrumbidgee Discovery Track.

name: Kambah Pool
note: Swimming spot: big boulders in the Murrumbidgee River, a 10-minute walk from the car park.

name: Red Rocks Gorge
note: Gorge: Murrumbidgee gorge and cliffs below the Bullen Range, walked on the track above it between Kambah Pool and Pine Island; cliff climbing is closed for peregrine falcon breeding.

name: Bullen Range Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: Bullen Range reserve with the Red Rocks cliff, a climbing site closed in part for peregrine falcon breeding.

name: Murrumbidgee Discovery Track
note: Long walk: 27 km track from Point Hut Crossing to Casuarina Sands, rated hard for its full length.

name: Murrumbidgee River Corridor
note: Linear reserve: 66 km of Murrumbidgee River land through the ACT, with its own access points (Casuarina Sands, Point Hut, Uriarra, Pine Island); a region of sites rather than one spot.

name: Lower Cotter Catchment Reserve
note: Catchment reserve: Parks ACT reserve on the lower Cotter; the visitor content read was limited.

name: Mount Stromlo Observatory
note: Observatory: Australia's astronomical research observatory on Mount Stromlo, rebuilt after the 2003 bushfires, with public star nights.

name: Stromlo Forest Park
note: Mountain-bike and forest park: one of the largest MTB parks close to a city, with west of Canberra.

name: ACT Bushfire Memorial
note: Memorial: 2006 memorial to the 2003 Canberra bushfires in Stromlo Forest Park, near the Cotter Road.

name: 2003 Canberra bushfires
note: Disaster site: the 2003 bushfires burned much of Namadgi and the western suburbs; the area's recovery is the subject of the bushfire memorial and the Stromlo Observatory rebuild.

name: National Arboretum Canberra
note: Arboretum: forest and tree collection on Forest Drive, with the Village Centre, bonsai collection and lookouts such as Dairy Farmers Hill.

name: Dairy Farmers Hill
note: Viewpoint: hill in the southwest of the National Arboretum with views over the forest and city.

name: Lindsay Pryor National Arboretum
note: Arboretum: smaller version of the National Arboretum, opposite it on Barrenjoey Drive.

name: National Zoo and Aquarium
note: Zoo: privately owned zoo and aquarium on Lady Denman Drive, beside Scrivener Dam, with koalas and native animals.

name: Scrivener Dam
note: Dam: 1963 dam across the Molonglo River that created Lake Burley Griffin, beside the National Zoo and Aquarium.

name: Stromlo Cottage
note: Historic cottage: 1926 officer's cottage in Coombs that now tells the story of the area's staff housing.

name: Jerrabomberra Wetlands
note: Wetland nature reserve: flat walking tracks with boardwalks, bird hides and interpretive signs beside the Molonglo River.

name: Jerrabomberra West Grasslands
note: Grassland walk: 8 km return Grassy Plains walk from the Callum Brae car park, about three hours.

name: Callum Brae
note: Heritage precinct: historic precinct on private land, the car park for the Grassy Plains walk; access is limited.

name: Mulligans Flat Woodland Sanctuary
note: Woodland sanctuary: 984-hectare reserve with walking, cycling and picnic areas, and the Wildbark visitor centre with a café.

name: Goorooyarroo Nature Reserve
note: Woodland reserve: adjoins Mulligans Flat, with walking tracks and picnic areas.

name: One Tree Hill Lookout
note: Lookout: Gungahlin lookout reached by walking from Hall, with views over Canberra on the Centenary Trail.

name: Centenary Trail
note: Long-distance trail: 145 km loop around Canberra, with a section climbing to One Tree Hill from Hall.

name: Lower Molonglo Water Quality Control Centre
wiki: Lower Molonglo Water Quality Control Centre
note: Wetlands: sewage treatment centre with wetlands and walking paths on the Molonglo; visitor value not confirmed by a visitor source.

name: Yarramundi Reach
note: River reach: Murrumbidgee reach at Yarramundi with a riverside park; listed on Wikipedia as a park.

name: Hall
note: Village: tiny heritage village of about 300 people with a heritage walk, cafés, a monthly market and access to the Hall wineries and One Tree Hill.

name: Hall Heritage Walk
note: Walk: National Trust heritage walk through Hall's historic houses and sites.

name: Hall School Museum and Heritage Centre
note: Museum: local museum in the former Hall Primary School with village history.

name: Hartley Hall Markets
note: Market: monthly Sunday market at the Hall Showground, from 9am to 2pm; a periodic market, not a permanent venue.

name: Hall Village Christmas Fair and Street Party
note: Event: annual Christmas fair and street party in Hall Heritage Village; an event, not a permanent spot.

name: Brindabella Hills Winery
note: Winery: cellar door on a ridge above the Murrumbidgee in Hall, with views and cool-climate wines, open weekends.

name: Local Spirit Distillery Cellar Door
note: Distillery cellar door: spirits tasting venue in Hall.

name: Pialligo Estate
note: Winery: cellar door and estate in Pialligo near the airport, one of the Canberra district's wineries; tastings by appointment.

name: Canberra District Wine Region
note: Wine region: the Canberra District wine region with 140 vineyards and cellar doors within 35 minutes of the city; a region rather than one spot.

name: Tharwa
note: Village: one of the original ACT settlements on the Murrumbidgee, the gateway to Namadgi and Tidbinbilla, with the old bridge.

name: Tharwa Bridge
note: Historic bridge: old bridge over the Murrumbidgee at Tharwa.

name: Cuppacumbalong Homestead
note: Homestead: historic homestead at Tharwa, one of the ACT's pastoral-era properties.

name: Cuppacumbalong Pottery
note: Pottery: pottery at the Cuppacumbalong estate in Tharwa.

name: Lanyon Homestead
note: Historic homestead: early Canberra settler's homestead with guided tours, walks, a garden and a café; closed Mondays.

name: Mugga-Mugga
note: Historic cottage: 1830s workers' cottage in Symonston with regular guided tours on set mornings.

name: Calthorpes' House
note: Historic house: early Canberra cottage with guided tours, part of the three-house pass with Lanyon and Mugga-Mugga.

name: Tuggeranong Homestead
note: Historic homestead: pastoral-era homestead in Richardson, now used for events and weddings.

name: Tuggeranong Schoolhouse Museum
note: Museum: 130-year-old schoolhouse in Chisholm with pastoral-era furniture and artefacts, open second Sundays.

name: Geoscience Australia Education Centre
note: Education centre: free geology and science displays with minerals, fossils and historic items in Symonston, open weekdays.

name: Lake Tuggeranong
note: Lake: artificial lake in Tuggeranong with a walk around its edge.

name: Tuggeranong Hill
note: Hill: prominent hill with a steep track to the summit and views over the Lanyon Valley and Tuggeranong.

name: Mount Wanniassa
note: Peak: 809 m mountain in the Wanniassa Hills Nature Reserve with walking trails on both slopes and views of Woden and Tuggeranong.

name: Murrumbidgee Country Club
note: Golf course: 18-hole course at the base of the Brindabellas at Kambah, open to public bookings.

name: Mount Ainslie
note: Peak: summit reached on foot, by bike or by car, with views over Lake Burley Griffin.

name: Red Hill Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: 3.2 km Red Track loop with the Red Hill Lookout over central Canberra.

name: Mount Majura
note: Peak: highest hill in northern Canberra at 888 m, with views over the bush capital; walking and cycling tracks.

name: Mount Pleasant Lookout
note: Lookout: lookout near the summit of Mount Pleasant over the reserve, Lake Burley Griffin and the Jerrabomberra Wetlands; also the Duntroon Dairy.

name: Black Mountain Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: bush reserve with many walking tracks and views over the city, reached from the Botanic Gardens.

name: Aranda Bushland Nature Reserve
note: Bushland reserve: Frost Hollow to Forest Walk of 1–2 hours from Caswell Drive.

name: O'Connor Ridge Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: 57-hectare reserve in O'Connor with access from Dryandra Street; small.

name: Rob Roy Range Nature Reserve
note: Nature reserve: large reserve with restricted access; much of it is leased land closed to the public.

name: Mount Taylor (Australian Capital Territory)
note: Peak: Mount Taylor, a volcanic hill in north Canberra listed on Wikipedia as a park; no visitor source read naming it.

name: Gold Creek Village
note: Village: Gungahlin village of specialty shops, family attractions and restaurants, the district's main visitor draw.

name: Cockington Green Gardens
note: Miniature village: miniature English village display in Nicholls, Gungahlin; open daily.

name: National Dinosaur Museum
note: Museum: a large collection of dinosaur and prehistoric fossil casts, Gold Creek Village, Nicholls; closed Fridays.

name: Gold Creek Country Club
note: Golf course: 18-hole championship course in Nicholls, Gungahlin.

name: Lake Ginninderra
note: Lake: artificial reservoir in Belconnen with a 7 km shared path around it.

name: Canberra Nature Park
note: Nature park: network of Canberra's urban bushland reserves that Parks ACT groups together.
